nodes.statement: A finite target-context law p(t,x) is fixed. The source sees T, the reader sees X, feedback B=g(X) has at most L labels and arrives before reply Z=f(T,B) with at most K labels; decoder sees X,B,Z and no uncounted current input.
nodes.scope: One finite classical trial; fixed target law, score, timing, boundary, policy class and alphabet cardinalities K,L>=1; independent random tapes. Contexts may have arbitrary finite positive support.

nodes.statement: Every deterministic source policy is represented by c(t)=(f(t,1),...,f(t,L)) in [K]^L; after choosing coordinate b, MAP decoding contributes the largest joint mass in each reply cell.
nodes.scope: R189:PROTOCOL; response coordinates are counterfactual policy entries, not all simultaneously transmitted symbols.

nodes.statement: S*(K,L)=max_c sum_x max_b sum_z max_{t in V_x:c_b(t)=z} p(t,x); deterministic policies attain it and independent randomization cannot improve it.
nodes.scope: Exactly R189:PROTOCOL; finite arbitrary candidate contexts; average success, not worst-case or experience.

nodes.statement: For m uniform three-candidate contexts with K=2,L=1, S*=2/3-q_min/(3m), where q_min is the minimum number of monochromatic contexts in a binary vertex coloring.
nodes.scope: Uniform incidence law on one finite 3-uniform hypergraph; one source-only binary reply.

nodes.statement: The displayed colorable and Fano systems each have seven vertices, seven uniform three-candidate contexts, degree three per target, uniform target/context marginals and posterior (1/3,1/3,1/3) in every context, while their incidence overlap differs.
nodes.scope: Only the listed summaries match; complete incidence laws and organizations do not.

nodes.statement: Under K=2,L=1 the colorable system attains 2/3, while the Fano system attains 13/21 because exactly one monochromatic context is unavoidable and sufficient.
nodes.scope: R189:MATCHED_PAIR under one common source-only binary encoder per system and the shared uniform scoring contract.

nodes.statement: Under K=2,L=2, explicit two-coordinate response words let both systems attain the local binary ceiling 2/3; feedback selects a nonmonochromatic coordinate before reply.
nodes.scope: A separate timely-feedback protocol instance; no binary reply can distinguish more than two of three positive candidates in one trial.

nodes.statement: The standard-library checker exhausts 33,024 response-vector assignments and passes 15 declared structural/value/boundary checks.
nodes.scope: Finite displayed systems only; code corroborates constructions and values but does not prove the general theorem or measure experience.

nodes.statement: A UCT application requires the same admitted actual process tokens, interval, complete signature, target/context carriers, consumer paths, access boundaries, timing and one type-invariant capability contract J.
nodes.scope: Actual application only; the mathematical hypergraphs and tests do not discharge these premises.

nodes.statement: If R189 actual grounding, C:FIXED_J and a genuine R189 capability difference hold for the same compared instances, inherited C:P1 entails different complete experiential structural types.
nodes.scope: Conditional type-level application only; no named feeling, intensity, subject count, exclusive owner or basal gate.

nodes.statement: Reflex and active-imagery twins can preserve the finite access contract, so the result alone does not identify doing, trying, agency or familiar mineness.
nodes.scope: Interpretive countercontrol; it does not assert actual deliberate/reflex/imagery systems share complete organization.

rules.statement: Represent the same permitted source strategy by its L-coordinate response vector.
rules.binding: One R189 finite trial with fixed law, target, score, alphabets, policy class, timing and information boundary.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: AND within this one typed protocol instance; distinct protocol comparisons are not conjoined.

rules.statement: Optimize MAP cell masses over reader coordinate choice and source response-vector assignments.
rules.binding: One R189 finite trial with the same p(t,x), K, L, timing, access and decoder target throughout.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: AND within this one typed protocol instance; distinct protocol comparisons are not conjoined.

rules.statement: Specialize one complete protocol instance to uniform three-candidate contexts with K=2,L=1.
rules.binding: One 3-uniform hypergraph, uniform incidence law, m contexts and one source-only binary reply.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: This is a specialization, not an added premise on arbitrary-context instances.

rules.statement: Apply the colorable witness and the Fano monochromatic-line obstruction under the shared declared summary contract.
rules.binding: Two separately complete seven-target protocol instances compared under one declared target/score/alphabet contract; matched summaries do not assert one system is both incidence structures.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: The A and Fano values are comparison branches, not simultaneous mechanisms in one token.

rules.statement: In the separately specified K=2,L=2 protocol, use explicit two-coordinate words and the local binary ceiling.
rules.binding: For each displayed context system separately, current context feedback arrives before the same trial's binary reply; compare this protocol to, but do not conjoin it with, K=2,L=1.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: L=1 and L=2 are alternative protocol instances under the same external target contract.

rules.statement: Apply inherited fixed-capability/type reasoning only after all same-instance actual premises are independently discharged.
rules.binding: One pair of actual comparison configurations with common complete signature, interval, ports, access/timing and one type-invariant J; the observed J difference must be the actual R189 result for those instances.
rules.alternative_route_semantics: No finite abstract witness or report substitutes for the full actual premise conjunction.

context_links.statement: The R188 pair-context cut is the two-candidate specialization of the response-vector formula; this is a contextual generalization relation, not a deduction from R188 alone.
Both require one common installed message/action rule; R189 adds a fixed finite-error and feedback-indexed application.
The higher-arity capability coordinate does not close the independently recorded familiar-mineness bridge.
